name: Xanadu
short_summary: Xanadu (founded 2016, Toronto) is the world's first publicly listed pure-play photonic quantum computing company (Nasdaq/TSX: XNDU, March 2026). It builds continuous-variable photonic quantum computers using GKP qubits in squeezed light: Borealis (2022) was the first cloud-accessible quantum advantage demonstration (Nature), and Aurora (2025, Nature) is the first modular networked photonic quantum computer with 12 logical qubits across four server racks. Xanadu also develops PennyLane (35,000+ active users), the most widely used open-source quantum ML framework. The company has raised $552M+, including a $302M SPAC listing, and is targeting a fault-tolerant photonic data centre by 2029.

short_summary: Pasqal (founded 2019, Massy, France) builds neutral-atom quantum computers using arrays of rubidium atoms held in optical tweezers and entangled through Rydberg interactions, supporting both analog quantum simulation and digital gate-based computing. name: QuiX Quantum
short_summary: QuiX Quantum (founded 2019, Enschede; University of Twente spin-out) is Europe's leading photonic quantum computing company, building universal quantum computers on ultra-low-loss silicon nitride (TriPleX) waveguide chips that operate at room temperature. It set a world record with its 20-mode photonic processor (validated in Quantum, 2023) and was the first company globally to sell a Universal Quantum Computer based on photonics — including a €14M contract with the German Aerospace Center (DLR, 2022). The company has raised €20.5M+ in VC funding (Seed €5.5M, Series A €15M) plus EIC Accelerator support. Founders include Dr. Jelmer Renema (Chief Scientist) and Dr. Hans van den Vlekkert; CEO is Dr. Stefan Hengesbach (former CEO of Q.ANT).

name: Google Quantum AI
short_summary: Google Quantum AI (founded 2012, Santa Barbara CA) is Alphabet's superconducting quantum computing division. It achieved quantum supremacy with the 53-qubit Sycamore processor in 2019, demonstrated below-threshold quantum error correction with the 105-qubit Willow chip in December 2024, and claimed verifiable quantum advantage with the Quantum Echoes algorithm in October 2025. The division operates its own qubit fabrication facility and publishes the open-source Cirq framework, pursuing a five-milestone roadmap toward commercially useful error-corrected quantum computation by 2029.

short_summary: Rigetti Computing (founded 2013, Berkeley CA; NASDAQ: RGTI) is a publicly traded superconducting quantum computing company that designs and fabricates its own processors at its Fab-1 facility in Fremont and delivers them via Quantum Cloud Services (QCS) and cloud marketplaces. It pioneered the Quil quantum instruction language and the Forest open-source SDK, went public via SPAC in March 2022, and has advanced through Aspen and Ankaa processor generations to the 108-qubit Cepheus-1 system (April 2026, 99.1% two-qubit CZ fidelity). In May 2026, Rigetti signed a letter of intent for up to $100 million in CHIPS Act funding from the U.S. Department of Commerce.

Quantum Cloud Services (QCS) delivers sub-millisecond classical-quantum latency, enabling hybrid quantum-classical workloads at speed
Cepheus-1-108Q (April 2026) achieves 99.9% single-qubit and 99.1% two-qubit CZ gate fidelity, marking a significant step toward fault-tolerant thresholds
Proprietary chiplet-based multi-die architecture (introduced Aspen-M, 2022) provides a credible scaling path to 1,000+ qubits without requiring a single larger die
Quil / PyQuil / Quilc open-source software stack enables pulse-level control via Quil-T, differentiating QCS from gate-only cloud services

name: ORCA Computing
short_summary: ORCA Computing (founded 2019, London; Oxford spin-out) builds room-temperature, rack-mounted photonic quantum computers based on time-bin multiplexed quantum memories. Its PT-1 was the first quantum computer sold to a national defence organisation (UK MoD, 2022), and its PT-2 (2024) delivers ~40 qumodes using deterministic single-photon sources with deep NVIDIA CUDA-Q integration. ORCA leads a £11.6M UK government quantum data centre consortium and has deployed systems at the UK NQCC, PCSS Poland, and Montana State University. Founders include Prof. Ian Walmsley (Oxford/Imperial), Dr. Richard Murray (CEO), and Dr. Josh Nunn (CSO, inventor of the ORCA memory).

differentiators: Room-temperature, rack-mounted operation using standard telecom-grade optical fibre components — no cryogenic cooling or vacuum required, enabling data-centre-ready deployment with a 19-inch rack form factor

Proprietary quantum memory technology (time-bin multiplexed photonic modes in quantum memories) invented at the University of Oxford NQIT Hub, enabling programmable boson sampling without the per-photon hardware overhead typical of linear-optical approaches

PT-2 (launched Oct 2024) uses deterministic single-photon sources (Sparrow Quantum chips) and delivers ~40 qumodes at industry-relevant clock cycles; estimated 4,000x more powerful than PT-1; first photonic system to combine multiple photon sources in one unit
First quantum computer sold to a national defence department — UK Ministry of Defence PT-1 deployment (June 2022); by early 2025 ORCA had delivered 10 on-premises PT-series systems globally
Deep integration with NVIDIA CUDA-Q and NVQLink (Oct 2025) enabling tightly coupled hybrid quantum-classical workflows within standard HPC/GPU data centre infrastructure

name: IBM Quantum
short_summary: IBM Quantum (est. 2016, Yorktown Heights NY) is IBM's quantum computing division operating the world's first public cloud quantum service (IBM Quantum Experience, 2016) and the largest fleet of superconducting processors. Its hardware roadmap progressed from 127-qubit Eagle (2021) through 433-qubit Osprey (2022) to 1,121-qubit Condor and 133-qubit Heron (2023), with Heron powering the modular IBM Quantum System Two. The division also publishes Qiskit, the most widely used open-source quantum SDK. IBM targets 200-qubit / 100 M-gate Starling by 2029 and a 2,000-qubit / 1 B-gate Blue Jay system by 2033.

Demonstrated evidence for quantum utility on a 127-qubit Eagle processor in Nature (June 2023), executing circuits beyond the reach of brute-force classical simulation
IBM Quantum System Two (Yorktown Heights, 2023) is the industry's first modular quantum computer, housing three Heron processors with a shared cryogenic infrastructure

short_summary: Oxford Quantum Circuits (OQC; founded 2017, Reading, UK) is a University of Oxford spin-out that builds and operates superconducting quantum computers for cloud delivery under a Quantum-Compute-as-a-Service model. name: Atom Computing
short_summary: Atom Computing (founded 2018, Berkeley CA) builds gate-based quantum computers using nuclear-spin qubits in optically trapped ytterbium-171 atoms. Its AC1000 system — the first to exceed 1,000 qubits in a gate-based platform (1,180 qubits announced October 2023) — features 1,200+ fully-connected physical qubits, all-to-all connectivity, single-qubit fidelity >99.9%, and on-premises or cloud (Azure Quantum) deployment. A Microsoft partnership (September 2024) demonstrated 24 entangled logical qubits on record; the companies are co-building the "Magne" system for Denmark. In May 2026, Atom signed a $100 million CHIPS Act Letter of Intent with the U.S. Department of Commerce.
